counterfactual_missing_items: No mention of systemic symptoms or family history of ocular melanocytosis or glaucoma
Absence of leptomeningeal vascular malformations on MRI makes Sturge-Weber syndrome less likely
decisive_items: Intraocular pressure measured by Icare tonometry was 22 mm Hg in the right eye and 12 mm Hg in the left.
Standard automated perimetry detected early visual-field defects in the right eye, and peripapillary OCT showed borderline retinal nerve-fibre-layer thickness on the right.
response.rationale: C1 is the champion because it accounts for both the ocular melanocytosis and glaucoma, which are supported by the patient's elevated intraocular pressure, visual field defects, and borderline retinal nerve-fibre-layer thickness. R4 is the runner-up as it only accounts for ocular melanocytosis without considering the glaucoma aspect.

rejected.why: R2 only accounts for glaucoma without considering the ocular melanocytosis aspect, which is also present in the patient's symptoms.
R3 is rejected due to the absence of leptomeningeal vascular malformations on MRI, which is a key feature of Sturge-Weber syndrome.
